subject: Engelska
title: Grammar: past simple
sourceSummary: Past tense in English: regular verbs with -ed, the most common irregular verbs, and did/didn't in questions and negative sentences.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Yesterday we ___ football in the park."
questions.opener: "Yesterday" means it has already happened. Regular verbs get a familiar ending in the past tense.
questions.explanation: "Yesterday" requires past simple. "Play" is a regular verb, so the past tense is formed with -ed: "played". "Plays" is present tense and does not fit with yesterday.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Last summer I ___ to Spain with my family."
questions.opener: "Go" is an irregular verb — it does not take an -ed ending.
questions.explanation: "Go" is irregular and becomes "went" in past simple. "Goed" does not exist in English — irregular verbs must be learned by heart.

questions.prompt: Which past simple form is correct?
questions.opener: Four common irregular verbs. Which line is correct?
questions.explanation: "Take" becomes "took" in the past tense. The others are irregular but are conjugated differently: have → had, see → saw, buy → bought. None of them take -ed.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct negative sentence: "I ___ my homework last night."
questions.opener: "Didn't" is used in the negative past tense. What happens to the main verb then?
questions.explanation: The negative past simple is formed with "didn't" + the verb in its base form: "I didn't do my homework". The past tense is already contained in "didn't", so the verb should not be conjugated a second time.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question: "___ you see the film last week?"
questions.opener: Questions in the past tense begin with an auxiliary verb — which one?
questions.explanation: "Last week" shows that it is the past tense, and then "Did" is used in the question: "Did you see...". After "did", the verb stands in its base form, so "see" and not "saw".

questions.prompt: Which time expression fits: "She watched a movie ___."
questions.opener: The verb is in the past tense — so the time expression must also point back in time.
questions.explanation: "Watched" is past simple, so the time expression must be about the past: "last night". "Every day" describes a habit and requires present simple: "She watches a movie every day".

questions.prompt: Correct the three errors: "Last weekend I go to my grandmother. We eat pizza and I didn't watched TV."
questions.opener: All the verbs should be in the past tense — but think about what happens after "didn't".
questions.answer: Last weekend I went to my grandmother. We ate pizza and I didn't watch TV.
steps: "Last weekend" is a past-time expression, so all the verbs in the text should be in past simple.
"I go" → "I went". "Go" is irregular: go → went.
"We eat" → "We ate". "Eat" is also irregular: eat → ate.
"I didn't watched" → "I didn't watch". After "didn't", the verb always stands in its base form.

questions.prompt: How do you form the past simple, and which common irregular verbs should you know?
questions.opener: One rule for regular verbs, a list for the irregular ones.
questions.answer: Regular verbs: verb + -ed (play → played, watch → watched, want → wanted) · if the verb ends in -e, -d is enough (like → liked) · consonant + y becomes -ied (study → studied). Common irregular verbs: go → went · have → had · see → saw · take → took · eat → ate · get → got · make → made · come → came · say → said · buy → bought. Questions: Did you play? · Negative: I didn't play · after did/didn't the verb always stands in its base form. Signal words: yesterday, last week, last summer, two days ago, in 2019.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "They ___ their rooms yesterday afternoon."
questions.opener: "Yesterday afternoon" means it already happened. "Clean" is a regular verb.
questions.explanation: "Yesterday afternoon" calls for past simple, and "clean" is regular: "cleaned". "Cleans" is present tense and doesn't fit with a past-time expression.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "She ___ a letter to her friend last week."
questions.opener: "Write" is irregular — it doesn't get an -ed ending.
questions.explanation: "Write" is irregular and becomes "wrote" in past simple. "Writed" doesn't exist in English, and "written" is a different form (past participle) not used in the simple past.

questions.prompt: Which past simple form is correct?
questions.opener: One of these verbs is spelled the same in the present and the past, but is pronounced differently.
questions.explanation: "Read" in the past tense is spelled the same as in the present (though pronounced "red" instead of "reed"). The others are irregular but change differently: give → gave, run → ran, drink → drank — none of them take -ed.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct negative sentence: "We ___ any time to visit the museum."
questions.opener: In negative past simple sentences, "didn't" is used. What happens to the main verb then?
questions.explanation: Negative past simple is formed with "didn't" + the verb in its base form: "We didn't have any time". The past tense is already in "didn't", so "have" shouldn't be inflected a second time.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question: "___ they win the match on Saturday?"
questions.opener: "On Saturday" here refers to a day that has already passed — which helping verb gives the question past tense?
questions.explanation: The question is about the past, so "Did" is used: "Did they win...". After "did", the verb stands in its base form, so "win" and not "won".

questions.prompt: Correct the three errors: "Last Friday I visit my cousin. We play video games and I didn't finished my homework."
questions.opener: All the verbs should be in the past tense — but think about what happens after "didn't".
questions.answer: Last Friday I visited my cousin. We played video games and I didn't finish my homework.
steps: "Last Friday" is a past-time expression, so all the verbs in the text should be in past simple.
"I visit" → "I visited". "Visit" is regular and gets -ed.
"We play" → "We played". "Play" is also regular and gets -ed.
"I didn't finished" → "I didn't finish". After "didn't", the verb always stands in its base form.

questions.prompt: Which time expression fits: "He called his friend ___."
questions.opener: The verb is in the past tense — so the time expression must also point back in time.
questions.explanation: "Called" is past simple, so the time expression must be about the past: "two days ago". "Every morning" describes a habit and calls for present simple: "He calls his friend every morning".
